A distant overview of Punchbowl National Cemetery. The runways of Honolulu International Airport are visible in the background as well.

My vantage point is the Tantalus, located in the hills just above Honolulu. The views are second to none, but the winds are quite fierce too.

images.filename: Honolulu as seen from the foot of Puaoaina - Punchbowl Hill, 1837 (PP-37-14-007).jpg
images.caption:
Linen-backed engraving of "Honolulu as seen from the foot of Puaoaina - Punchbowl Hill" (Puowaina, Punch Bowl Crater), 1837, with inset of Female Seminary, Wailuku. 1 art print : engraving, b&w ; 33 x 53 cm.
Nathan Van Patten, wrote in Early Native Engravers of Hawaii (1926):

This is one of the earliest views of Honolulu, which at this time consisted of a rambling assemblage of native buildings with a fringe of more pretentious buildings of American type along the water-front. There is one church visible and to be distinguished by its steeple, also two large buildings each with a flagstaff and flags flying therefrom. Several sailing ships are in the harbor, and a nest of masts looms up from behind a group of larger buildings near the head of the bay. Very little vegetation is shown in this plate. There are two groups of palms beside the shore. At the left center are two oddly drawn prancing horses with riders and a native burden-carrier.
images.alt:
Linen-backed engraving of "Honolulu as seen from the foot of Puaoaina - Punchbowl Hill" (Puowaina, Punch Bowl Crater), 1837, with inset of Female Seminary, Wailuku. 1 art print : engraving, b&w ; 33 x 53 cm.

images.filename: Edward Belcher, View of Honolulu, Oahu, Sandwich Islands.jpg
images.caption: View of Honolulu, Oahu, Sandwich Islands. Described as one of the most attractive of all nineteenth-century views of Honolulu. The fort is prominently featured in the right middle ground, with ships at anchor and Punchbowl in the distance. At the right is Nuuanu valley.
images.alt: View of Honolulu, Oahu, Sandwich Islands. Described as one of the most attractive of all nineteenth-century views of Honolulu. The fort is prominently featured in the right middle ground, with ships at anchor and Punchbowl in the distance. At the right is Nuuanu valley.
